For individuals with amblyopia (lazy eye), it is possible for their vision to recover in one of the affected eyes over time. This recovery occurs after visual loss in the other eye has stabilized and is no longer progressing.

More specifically, studies suggest that older adults who develop amblyopia can experience some degree of improvement or "recovery" of vision in the previously normal eye, but this process typically takes several years to a decade or more. The underlying cause of this recovery remains unclear, but it's thought to involve factors such as changes in the brain or visual system that occur after the initial injury.

However, it's essential to note that not everyone with amblyopia will experience significant improvement in their vision, and some individuals may continue to have impaired vision in one eye. Additionally, any improvements in vision should be evaluated by an eye care professional to rule out underlying conditions that could be contributing to the loss of vision.
